sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好你好，欢迎收听 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: The show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 在这档节目里，你可以听引人入胜的故事，了解这个世界奇妙又有趣的一面，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about one of the most famous and controversial psychological experiments of all time, the Stanford Prison Experiment.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊聊史上最著名、也最具争议的心理学实验之一——斯坦福监狱实验。

sentences.en: To some observers, it was seen as yet more proof of how otherwise law-abiding, normal humans can do horrific things to each other.
sentences.zh: 在一些观察者看来，这又一次证明了原本守法、正常的人，也可能对彼此做出可怕的事情。

sentences.en: So in this episode, we’ll talk about the purpose of the experiment, what actually happened, what it tells us about human psychology, and why its greatest critics think it doesn’t really tell us that much at all.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一集里，我们会聊聊这个实验的目的、实际发生了什么、它揭示了哪些人类心理层面的东西，以及为什么它最严厉的批评者认为，它其实什么都说明不了。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it and talk about the Stanford Prison Experiment.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们就直接进入正题，聊聊斯坦福监狱实验。

sentences.en: An unfortunate truth about humanity is that we humans are capable of committing acts against our fellow humans that are utterly inhumane.
sentences.zh: 关于人性，有一个令人遗憾的事实：人类有能力对同类做出极其残忍、毫无人性的事情。

sentences.en: Men and women, who might otherwise live normal, kind lives, under certain conditions, sometimes do horrific things.
sentences.zh: 那些原本可能过着正常、善良生活的男男女女，在某些特定条件下，有时也会做出可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, we have tens of thousands of years of human history that shows this to be true, it is still the case today, and no doubt it will still be the case in thousands of years to come.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，人类几万年的历史都证明了这一点，今天依然如此，毫无疑问，未来几千年也依然会是如此。

sentences.en: But…why? What is it about certain situations that can change a person’s behaviour?
sentences.zh: 但是……为什么会这样？究竟是某些情境中的什么东西，能够改变一个人的行为？

sentences.en: Can otherwise normal, rational people, be turned into monsters, if placed in particular circumstances?
sentences.zh: 原本正常、理性的人，如果被置于特定的环境中，会不会变成怪物？

sentences.en: In August of 1971, a Stanford professor named Philip Zimbardo sought to answer this question.
sentences.zh: 1971 年 8 月，斯坦福大学一位名叫 Philip Zimbardo 的教授，试图回答这个问题。

sentences.en: He put out an advertisement in the local newspaper, which read:
sentences.zh: 他在当地报纸上登了一则广告，内容是：

sentences.en: Philip Zimbardo's advert: Male college students needed for psychological study of prison life. $15 per day for one to two weeks, beginning August 14th.
sentences.zh: Philip Zimbardo 的广告：招募男大学生参与监狱生活心理学研究，为期一到两周，每天 15 美元,8 月 14 日开始。

sentences.en: Slightly ominous. Now, $15 in 1971 is around $110 in today’s money.
sentences.zh: 听起来有点不祥。1971 年的 15 美元，换算成今天大约是 110 美元。

sentences.en: Not a colossal amount of money, by Californian standards at least, but enough to attract a few university students to participate in a “psychological study of prison life”.
sentences.zh: 以加州的标准来说，这不算一笔巨款，但足以吸引一些大学生来参加这场“监狱生活心理学研究”。

sentences.en: 75 students applied. They were interviewed, screened to check that they didn’t have any serious medical problems, any psychological conditions, or a criminal record.
sentences.zh: 有 75 名学生报名。他们接受了面试和筛选，以确认没有严重的身体疾病、心理问题或犯罪记录。

sentences.en: In other words, they needed to be regular university students.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们需要是普通的大学生。

sentences.en: The group was whittled down to 24 participants, who were split into two groups.
sentences.zh: 最终筛选出 24 名参与者，被分成两组。

sentences.en: Half were randomly assigned to be guards, and half were assigned to be prisoners.
sentences.zh: 一半人被随机分配当狱警，另一半被分配当囚犯。

sentences.en: These 24 young men, all considered to be healthy, well-adjusted, and average in almost every way, were ready to begin the experiment.
sentences.zh: 这 24 名年轻男性都被认为身心健康、适应良好，各方面都很普通，他们已经准备好开始这场实验。

sentences.en: The “guards” were asked to report to Stanford University on the first day of the experiment to begin their training and orientation.
sentences.zh: “狱警”们被要求在实验第一天到斯坦福大学报到，开始接受培训和岗前指导。

sentences.en: They were given uniforms, batons, and reflective sunglasses to wear, along with instructions on their role: to maintain order in the prison.
sentences.zh: 他们领到了制服、警棍和反光墨镜，并被告知自己的职责：维持监狱秩序。

sentences.en: The “prisoners,” however, were told to wait at home for further instructions.
sentences.zh: 而“囚犯”们则被告知在家等待进一步通知。

sentences.en: What they didn’t know was that their participation would begin with a surprise arrest.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道的是，自己的参与将以一场突如其来的“逮捕”拉开序幕。

sentences.en: Without any warning, real police officers—yes, actual police officers— showed up at their homes.
sentences.zh: 毫无预警地，真正的警察——没错，是真正的警察——出现在了他们家门口。

sentences.en: They were “arrested,” handcuffed, and taken to a police station.
sentences.zh: 他们被“逮捕”、戴上手铐，押送到警察局。

sentences.en: There, they were fingerprinted, photographed, and charged with offences like armed robbery.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他们被采集指纹、拍照，并被指控犯下持械抢劫之类的罪名。

sentences.en: Of course, the charges weren’t real, and the participants knew they were part of an experiment.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些指控都不是真的，参与者也知道自己是在参加一场实验。

sentences.en: But the realistic nature of the arrest was designed to make them feel as though they had truly lost their freedom.
sentences.zh: 但这场逮捕的逼真程度，是刻意设计来让他们感觉自己真的失去了自由。

sentences.en: After this mock arrest process, the prisoners were blindfolded and transported to the basement of Stanford University’s psychology building, which had been transformed into a makeshift prison.
sentences.zh: 经过这场模拟逮捕后，囚犯们被蒙上眼睛，送往斯坦福大学心理学系大楼的地下室——那里已经被改造成一座临时监狱。

sentences.en: When they arrived, their blindfolds were removed, and they were made to strip down, sprayed with what was described as a “delousing spray,” and given prison uniforms to wear.
sentences.zh: 抵达后，他们的眼罩被摘下，被要求脱光衣服，喷上所谓的“除虱喷雾”，然后换上囚服。

sentences.en: The uniforms were simple but designed to be humiliating.
sentences.zh: 囚服很简单，但设计上刻意带有羞辱性。

sentences.en: Prisoners wore smocks, which were like long, shapeless dresses, and on their heads, they had to wear a nylon stocking cap.
sentences.zh: 囚犯们穿着罩衫，就像没有版型的长袍，头上还得戴一顶尼龙丝袜帽。

sentences.en: Around their ankles, they had chains that rattled as they walked, a constant reminder of their lack of freedom.
sentences.zh: 脚踝上戴着锁链，走路时会哗啦作响，时刻提醒着他们失去了自由。

sentences.en: Each prisoner was assigned a number, which was sewn onto their uniform.
sentences.zh: 每个囚犯都被分配了一个编号，缝在囚服上。

sentences.en: From that point on, they were no longer addressed by their names but only by their numbers.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他们不再被人以姓名相称，只被叫编号。

sentences.en: This was all intentional. The idea was to make them feel like they had lost their identity and their individuality.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是刻意为之，目的是让他们觉得自己失去了身份和个性。

sentences.en: Now, on the other side of this “prison” were the guards.
sentences.zh: 而在这座“监狱”的另一边，是狱警们。

sentences.en: The guards were dressed in khaki uniforms, they had reflective sunglasses to make eye contact impossible, and were carrying batons —though they were told not to use them for physical punishment.
sentences.zh: 狱警们穿着卡其色制服，戴着反光墨镜让人无法与他们进行眼神交流，还带着警棍——不过他们被告知不能用警棍施加体罚。

sentences.en: The guards had been given a very simple instruction: maintain order in the prison.
sentences.zh: 狱警们得到的指示非常简单：维持监狱秩序。

sentences.en: Beyond that, they were largely left to figure things out for themselves.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，基本上就靠他们自己摸索了。

sentences.en: And at first, things were relatively calm.
sentences.zh: 起初，情况相对平静。

sentences.en: The prisoners followed the guards’ instructions, the guards kept watch, and Zimbardo and his team observed everything from behind hidden cameras and microphones.
sentences.zh: 囚犯们听从狱警的指示，狱警负责看守，Zimbardo 和他的团队则通过隐藏的摄像头和麦克风观察着一切。

sentences.en: But it didn’t take long for things to spiral out of control.
sentences.zh: 但没过多久，事情就开始失控。

sentences.en: On just the second day, the prisoners rebelled.
sentences.zh: 仅仅到了第二天，囚犯们就开始反抗。

sentences.en: They tore off their numbers, refused to leave their cells, and shouted at the guards.
sentences.zh: 他们撕掉编号，拒绝走出牢房，还对狱警大喊大叫。

sentences.en: The guards, who had been unsure of their authority at first, suddenly became much more aggressive.
sentences.zh: 原本对自己权威还有点没底的狱警们，突然变得咄咄逼人起来。

sentences.en: They used fire extinguishers to force prisoners back into their cells.
sentences.zh: 他们用灭火器把囚犯逼回牢房。

sentences.en: They stripped some prisoners naked as a form of humiliation.
sentences.zh: 他们把一些囚犯的衣服扒光，作为一种羞辱手段。

sentences.en: And they began to enforce strict rules—rules that seemed to come out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 他们还开始执行一些严苛的规矩——那些规矩似乎凭空冒出来的。

sentences.en: For example, prisoners were only allowed to go to the toilet at certain times.
sentences.zh: 比如，囚犯只被允许在特定时间上厕所。

sentences.en: If they broke the rules or annoyed the guards, they were punished.
sentences.zh: 如果谁违反规定或惹恼了狱警，就会受到惩罚。

sentences.en: Some were forced to do physical exercises like push-ups.
sentences.zh: 有的人被逼着做俯卧撑之类的体能训练。

sentences.en: Others were put into solitary confinement —a tiny, dark closet that could barely fit one person.
sentences.zh: 还有的人被关进单人禁闭室——一个几乎只能容下一个人的狭小黑暗小隔间。

sentences.en: And as the days went on, the punishments became more creative…and cruel.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，惩罚手段变得越来越“有创意”……也越来越残忍。

sentences.en: One guard made prisoners clean the toilets with their bare hands.
sentences.zh: 有个狱警让囚犯徒手清洗马桶。

sentences.en: Another forced them to simulate sexual acts as a way of degrading them.
sentences.zh: 还有人逼他们模拟性行为，以此来羞辱他们。

sentences.en: What was shocking is that none of this was planned.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的是，这一切都不是事先安排好的。

sentences.en: The guards came up with these punishments on their own as if the power they had been given unleashed something darker inside them.
sentences.zh: 这些惩罚都是狱警自己想出来的，仿佛他们被赋予的权力，释放出了他们内心深处更黑暗的一面。

sentences.en: As for the prisoners, they quickly fell into the roles that had been assigned to them.
sentences.zh: 至于囚犯们，他们很快就陷入了被分配给自己的角色之中。

sentences.en: Some became passive, obeying every command without question.
sentences.zh: 有些人变得被动顺从，对每一个命令都言听计从。

sentences.en: Others broke down emotionally, crying and screaming to be let out.
sentences.zh: 有些人则情绪崩溃，又哭又喊，求着要被放出去。

sentences.en: One prisoner, referred to only as Prisoner 8612, began to have what seemed like a complete mental breakdown after just 36 hours.
sentences.zh: 有一名囚犯，只被称作 8612 号囚犯，在短短 36 小时后就出现了近乎彻底的精神崩溃。

sentences.en: He screamed at the guards, yelled that he wanted to leave, and even told Zimbardo that he felt like he was losing his mind.
sentences.zh: 他对着狱警尖叫，大喊自己想离开，甚至告诉 Zimbardo，他感觉自己快要疯了。

sentences.en: Instead of ending the experiment, Zimbardo initially tried to convince him to stay, saying that leaving would disappoint the others.
sentences.zh: Zimbardo 起初并没有终止实验，反而试图说服他留下来，说他离开会让其他人失望。

sentences.en: But eventually, Prisoner 8612 was allowed to go.
sentences.zh: 但最终,8612 号囚犯还是被允许离开了。

sentences.en: After Prisoner 8612 was released, you might think that things would have settled down.
sentences.zh: 8612 号囚犯获释后，你可能以为局面会平静下来。

sentences.en: But instead, the opposite happened. The guards became even harsher.
sentences.zh: 但恰恰相反，情况变得更糟。狱警变得更加严厉。

sentences.en: It was as though they felt their authority had been challenged, and they needed to reassert control over the prisoners.
sentences.zh: 仿佛他们觉得自己的权威受到了挑战，必须重新对囚犯确立控制。

sentences.en: One of the ways they did this was by targeting the prisoners who they saw as leaders—those who were more likely to resist.
sentences.zh: 他们其中一种做法，是专门针对那些他们视为“带头人”的囚犯——那些更可能反抗的人。

sentences.en: The guards singled them out for extra punishment, like longer periods in solitary confinement or forcing them to do degrading tasks.
sentences.zh: 狱警对这些人格外惩罚，比如延长单独禁闭的时间，或逼他们做有辱人格的事情。

sentences.en: And while some prisoners resisted, others started to turn on each other.
sentences.zh: 在一些囚犯继续反抗的同时，另一些人则开始互相背叛。

sentences.en: Zimbardo and his team had planted the idea that some prisoners might be secretly working with the guards, acting as informants.
sentences.zh: Zimbardo 和他的团队故意散布了一种想法，说某些囚犯可能暗中与狱警合作，充当告密者。

sentences.en: This led to paranoia and division among the prisoners.
sentences.zh: 这在囚犯之间引发了猜疑和分裂。

sentences.en: Instead of uniting against the guards, they became suspicious of one another, which made them easier to control.
sentences.zh: 他们没有团结起来对抗狱警，反而彼此猜忌，这让他们更容易被控制。

sentences.en: Now, let’s stop for a moment and remember that all of the participants, both the guards and the prisoners, knew that this was a simulation, that they weren’t really inside a prison, and it was all an experiment.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们先停一下，回想一下：所有参与者，不管是狱警还是囚犯，都清楚这是一场模拟，他们并不是真的身处监狱，这一切都只是一场实验。

sentences.en: But on both sides, something about this situation and its power imbalance, one group in control and the other being subjugated, this seemed to flip something in their minds and make them almost forget that it wasn’t real.
sentences.zh: 但对双方来说，这种情境以及其中的权力失衡——一方掌控、另一方被压制——似乎在他们心里触发了某种开关，让他们几乎忘记了这一切并不是真的。

sentences.en: And day by day, the prison environment became more and more oppressive.
sentences.zh: 监狱里的氛围一天比一天压抑。

sentences.en: The guards introduced something they called “privilege cells.”
sentences.zh: 狱警引入了一种他们称之为“特权牢房”的制度。

sentences.en: Prisoners in these cells were given slightly better treatment—they could eat better food, or they didn’t have to wear chains.
sentences.zh: 住在这些牢房里的囚犯会得到稍好一点的待遇——比如能吃到更好的食物，或者不用戴锁链。

sentences.en: But to stay in the privilege cell, prisoners had to obey the guards without question.
sentences.zh: 但要想留在特权牢房，囚犯就必须无条件服从狱警。

sentences.en: This was a psychological tactic. It created jealousy and mistrust among the prisoners, breaking down any sense of solidarity they might have had.
sentences.zh: 这是一种心理战术，在囚犯之间制造了嫉妒和猜忌，瓦解了他们本可能拥有的团结感。

sentences.en: By the fourth day, the situation had grown even darker.
sentences.zh: 到了第四天，情况变得更加黑暗。

sentences.en: One prisoner, referred to as Prisoner 819, had an emotional breakdown.
sentences.zh: 有一名被称作 819 号囚犯的人，情绪彻底崩溃。

sentences.en: He cried uncontrollably and refused to eat.
sentences.zh: 他止不住地哭泣，还拒绝进食。

sentences.en: Zimbardo and his team decided to let him leave the experiment.
sentences.zh: Zimbardo 和他的团队决定让他退出实验。

sentences.en: But as he was preparing to go, something strange happened.
sentences.zh: 但就在他准备离开的时候，发生了一件奇怪的事。

sentences.en: While Prisoner 819 was in another room, one of the guards made the other prisoners chant: “Prisoner #819 is a bad prisoner.
sentences.zh: 819 号囚犯待在另一个房间时，一名狱警让其他囚犯一起喊口号：“819 号囚犯是个坏囚犯。

sentences.en: Because of what Prisoner 819 did, my cell is a mess, Mr.
sentences.zh: 因为 819 号囚犯做的事，我的牢房乱成一团，

sentences.en: Correctional Officer.” Hearing this, Prisoner 819 broke down even further.
sentences.zh: 长官。”听到这些,819 号囚犯情绪崩溃得更厉害了。

sentences.en: He felt overwhelming guilt and begged to return to the prison to prove he wasn’t a bad prisoner.
sentences.zh: 他感到无比愧疚，恳求回到监狱，证明自己不是个坏囚犯。

sentences.en: Zimbardo had to step in. He reminded Prisoner 819 that he wasn’t a real prisoner, that this was just an experiment, and that he could leave whenever he wanted.
sentences.zh: Zimbardo 不得不出面干预，提醒 819 号囚犯，他并不是真正的囚犯，这只是一场实验，他随时都可以离开。

sentences.en: Only then did Prisoner 819 agree to walk.
sentences.zh: 819 号囚犯这才同意离开。

sentences.en: For Zimbardo, this moment was a wake-up call.
sentences.zh: 对 Zimbardo 来说，这一刻是一记警钟。

sentences.en: The line between reality and the roles they were playing had become dangerously blurred.
sentences.zh: 现实与他们所扮演角色之间的界限，已经模糊到了危险的地步。

sentences.en: The final turning point came when one of Zimbardo’s graduate students and his future wife, Christina Maslach, visited the prison on the sixth day.
sentences.zh: 最后的转折点出现在第六天，Zimbardo 的一名研究生、也是他未来的妻子 Christina Maslach，来监狱进行了探访。

sentences.en: Maslach had come to observe the experiment.
sentences.zh: Maslach 本是来观察这场实验的。

sentences.en: But what she saw shocked her. She watched as the guards humiliated the prisoners, screaming at them and making them perform degrading tasks.
sentences.zh: 但她所看到的一切让她感到震惊。她目睹狱警羞辱囚犯，对他们大吼大叫，逼他们做有辱人格的事情。

sentences.en: She confronted Zimbardo and demanded to know how he could allow this to continue.
sentences.zh: 她当面质问 Zimbardo，要求他解释自己怎么能允许这种情况继续下去。

sentences.en: Maslach told him that the experiment was unethical and that the prisoners were suffering real harm.
sentences.zh: Maslach 告诉他，这场实验不道德，囚犯们正在遭受真实的伤害。

sentences.en: At first, Zimbardo resisted. He argued that the experiment was revealing important truths about human behaviour.
sentences.zh: 起初，Zimbardo 并不认同，他辩称这场实验正在揭示人类行为中一些重要的真相。

sentences.en: But then, he realised that he had become part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 但随后，他意识到自己已经成了问题的一部分。

sentences.en: He wasn’t just an observer—he was acting like the prison warden, and it was he who was enabling and encouraging the guards’ abusive behaviour.
sentences.zh: 他已经不只是一个观察者——他的行为更像是监狱长，正是他在放任并助长狱警的虐待行为。

sentences.en: As the designer of the experiment, he should have been a neutral observer, but he was an active participant.
sentences.zh: 作为实验的设计者，他本应是一个中立的观察者，但他却成了一个积极的参与者。

sentences.en: That same night, Zimbardo made the decision to end the experiment.
sentences.zh: 就在当天晚上，Zimbardo 做出了终止实验的决定。

sentences.en: It had been planned to last for two weeks, but it was stopped after just six days.
sentences.zh: 这场实验原计划持续两周，但只进行了六天就被叫停。

sentences.en: When the experiment was over, Zimbardo and his team reflected on what they had seen.
sentences.zh: 实验结束后，Zimbardo 和他的团队对所目睹的一切进行了反思。

sentences.en: The results seemed to show that ordinary people could quickly conform to roles of authority or submission, even in a short period of time.
sentences.zh: 结果似乎表明，普通人即便在很短的时间内，也会迅速顺应权威或服从的角色。

sentences.en: The guards, many of whom had never shown signs of cruelty before, became aggressive and sadistic.
sentences.zh: 许多此前从未表现出残忍倾向的狱警，变得咄咄逼人、甚至带有虐待倾向。

sentences.en: The prisoners, who were healthy and confident at the start, became passive, anxious, and even traumatised.
sentences.zh: 而那些一开始健康又自信的囚犯，则变得被动、焦虑，甚至留下了心理创伤。

sentences.en: Zimbardo called this the power of the “situation.” He argued that it wasn’t that the guards were bad people but that the situation itself brought out bad behaviour.
sentences.zh: Zimbardo 把这称为“情境”的力量。他认为，并不是狱警本身是坏人，而是情境本身激发出了恶劣的行为。

sentences.en: It was a convenient explanation and would help rationalise the behaviour of things like prison guards in Nazi concentration camps, and later on, would be used to explain the atrocities at Abu Ghraib prison in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 这是一种很方便的解释，后来被用来为纳粹集中营看守的行为做合理化解释，再往后，又被用来解释伊拉克阿布格莱布监狱的暴行。

sentences.en: It was not the people who were fundamentally evil, but that the nature of the situation brought out this capacity for evil that exists within us.
sentences.zh: 并不是这些人骨子里就邪恶，而是特定情境的本质，激发出了我们每个人内心都潜藏着的作恶能力。

sentences.en: But not everyone agreed with Zimbardo’s conclusions.
sentences.zh: 但并不是所有人都认同 Zimbardo 的结论。

sentences.en: And especially in recent years, the Stanford Prison Experiment has faced a lot of criticism.
sentences.zh: 尤其是近些年，斯坦福监狱实验受到了大量批评。

sentences.en: First of all, many people have questioned the scientific validity of the experiment.
sentences.zh: 首先，很多人质疑这项实验在科学上的有效性。

sentences.en: For an experiment to be scientifically valid, it needs to be carefully controlled, with clear instructions and procedures.
sentences.zh: 一项实验要具备科学有效性，就需要经过严谨的控制，有清晰的指令和流程。

sentences.en: However, critics argue that Zimbardo didn’t do this.
sentences.zh: 然而，批评者认为 Zimbardo 并没有做到这一点。

sentences.en: For example, the guards were not given strict guidelines on how to behave, and some say that Zimbardo encouraged them to act more aggressively.
sentences.zh: 比如，狱警们并没有得到关于该如何行事的严格准则，还有人说 Zimbardo 曾鼓励他们表现得更具攻击性。

sentences.en: One former guard, in an interview years later, said that Zimbardo had given them the impression that they were supposed to make life difficult for the prisoners.
sentences.zh: 多年后，一名曾经的狱警在采访中表示，Zimbardo 给他们的印象是，他们应该让囚犯的日子不好过。

sentences.en: This has led some to argue that the experiment wasn’t really observing natural behaviour—it was almost like a performance, with the guards trying to live up to what they thought Zimbardo wanted.
sentences.zh: 这让一些人认为，这场实验其实观察到的并不是自然行为，更像是一场表演，狱警们努力去迎合他们以为 Zimbardo 想要看到的东西。

sentences.en: Another related criticism is that the participants knew they were in an experiment.
sentences.zh: 另一个相关的批评是，参与者自己知道他们身处一场实验之中。

sentences.en: They were university students, not professional prison guards or actual prisoners.
sentences.zh: 他们只是大学生，并不是职业狱警，也不是真正的囚犯。

sentences.en: Critics argue that the participants might have been exaggerating their behaviour because they felt like they were playing a role, like they were expected to behave in a certain way, and therefore, that’s what they did.
sentences.zh: 批评者认为，参与者可能夸大了自己的行为表现，因为他们觉得自己是在扮演一个角色，觉得别人期待他们以某种特定方式行事，于是他们就那样做了。

sentences.en: Given that they had no criminal record and no direct experience of prison, their only point of reference would probably have been prison movies, so one criticism is that they would have based their behaviour on what they had seen in films, which of course, is not a truly accurate representation of prison life.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他们没有犯罪记录，也没有直接接触过监狱的经历，他们唯一的参照物很可能就是监狱题材的电影，所以有一种批评认为，他们的行为其实是照着电影里看到的东西来演的，而这当然并不能真实、准确地反映监狱生活。

sentences.en: And on the subject of truly representing real life, there is the criticism that the participants in the experiment didn’t accurately reflect real-life prisons.
sentences.zh: 说到真实反映现实生活这一点，还有一种批评是，实验参与者并不能准确代表现实中的监狱情况。

sentences.en: Real guards and prisoners come from very different backgrounds and have very different motivations.
sentences.zh: 现实中的狱警和囚犯，来自截然不同的背景，也有着截然不同的动机。

sentences.en: All the guards and all the prisoners were white, middle-class, psychologically healthy university students, and that simply isn’t a representative sample of a prison, let alone society more widely.
sentences.zh: 而实验中所有的狱警和囚犯，都是白人、中产阶级、心理健康的大学生，这根本无法代表监狱的真实构成，更别提代表更广泛的社会了。

sentences.en: And then there’s the question of ethics.
sentences.zh: 接下来是伦理层面的问题。

sentences.en: Today, the Stanford Prison Experiment would never be allowed to happen.
sentences.zh: 放到今天，斯坦福监狱实验根本不可能被允许进行。

sentences.en: Modern ethical guidelines for psychological experiments would see it as far too harmful.
sentences.zh: 按照现代心理学实验的伦理准则，这场实验的危害性实在太大了。

sentences.en: The participants were subjected to extreme stress, humiliation, and emotional trauma —all things that researchers today are required to avoid.
sentences.zh: 参与者承受了极端的压力、羞辱和情感创伤——这些都是今天的研究者被要求必须避免的。

sentences.en: In fact, after the Stanford Prison Experiment, the field of psychology tightened its rules for what could and couldn’t be done in experiments.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在斯坦福监狱实验之后，心理学界收紧了关于实验中哪些事可以做、哪些不可以做的规定。

sentences.en: Researchers now have to ensure the safety and well-being of their participants, and they must get approval from ethics committees before starting any study.
sentences.zh: 如今，研究者必须确保参与者的安全和福祉，而且在开展任何研究之前，都必须获得伦理委员会的批准。

sentences.en: Finally, there’s the question of what the experiment actually tells us.
sentences.zh: 最后，还有一个问题是，这场实验到底告诉了我们什么。

sentences.en: Zimbardo argued that it showed how ordinary people could commit cruel acts when placed in certain situations.
sentences.zh: Zimbardo 认为，它表明普通人在特定情境下，也可能做出残忍的行为。

sentences.en: However, critics have said this conclusion is too simplistic.
sentences.zh: 然而，批评者认为这个结论过于简单化了。

sentences.en: Human behaviour is complex, and the experiment doesn’t account for other factors like personality, individual morality, or personal choice.
sentences.zh: 人类行为是复杂的，而这场实验并没有考虑到其他因素，比如个性、个人道德或个人选择。

sentences.en: Yes, this experiment shows that people can behave in unusual ways in unusual situations, but it is not definitive proof of anything.
sentences.zh: 没错，这场实验确实表明，人在不寻常的情境下会做出不寻常的行为，但它并不能确凿地证明任何事情。

sentences.en: Despite its flaws, the Stanford Prison Experiment has had a huge impact on how we think about human behaviour, power, and authority.
sentences.zh: 尽管存在种种缺陷，斯坦福监狱实验依然对我们理解人类行为、权力和权威的方式产生了巨大影响。

sentences.en: It’s still widely discussed in psychology classes around the world, often as an example of both the power of social roles and the dangers of unethical research.
sentences.zh: 如今它仍在世界各地的心理学课堂上被广泛讨论，常常被用作社会角色力量以及不道德研究之危险的双重例证。

sentences.en: The experiment also raised important questions about the systems and structures we create as a society.
sentences.zh: 这场实验也提出了一些重要问题，关于我们作为一个社会所创建的种种体制和结构。

sentences.en: It highlighted how institutions —whether prisons, workplaces, or even schools—can shape the behaviour of the people within them.
sentences.zh: 它揭示了各种机构——不管是监狱、职场，还是学校——是如何塑造身处其中之人的行为的。

sentences.en: So, to wrap things up, what can we take away from the Stanford Prison Experiment?
sentences.zh: 那么，总结一下，我们能从斯坦福监狱实验中学到什么呢？

sentences.en: At the very least, it’s a reminder of how much our environment and social roles can influence the way we act.
sentences.zh: 至少，它提醒了我们，环境和社会角色对我们行为方式的影响有多大。

sentences.en: It shows us that even ordinary people can behave in extraordinary ways—sometimes for the worse—when placed in situations of power or control.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们，即便是普通人，一旦被置于掌权或受控的情境中，也可能做出不寻常的举动——有时是往坏的方向发展。

sentences.en: But it’s also a reminder to be critical.
sentences.zh: 但它同时也提醒我们要保持批判性思维。

sentences.en: Not everything we see, even in famous experiments, is quite as straightforward as it seems.
sentences.zh: 我们所看到的一切，哪怕是著名的实验，也未必真的像表面上看起来那么简单直接。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on The Stanford Prison Experiment, one of the most famous psychological experiments of all time, but also one of the most controversial.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天这期关于斯坦福监狱实验的节目就到这里，它是史上最著名的心理学实验之一，同时也是争议最大的实验之一。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这一期节目有什么看法。

sentences.en: What conclusions do you think we can draw from this experiment, if any?
sentences.zh: 你觉得我们能从这场实验中得出什么结论，如果有的话？

sentences.en: Does it tell us anything we didn’t know already, or is it yet another reminder of how complex human behaviour is, and we shouldn’t read too much into it?
sentences.zh: 它是否告诉了我们一些我们原本不知道的事情，还是说，它只是又一次提醒我们人类行为有多复杂，我们不该过度解读？

sentences.en: I would love to know, so let’s get this discussion started.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道答案，所以我们就来开启这场讨论吧。

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接前往我们的社区论坛 community.leonardoenglish.com，和其他同样充满好奇心的朋友们聊起来。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 以上就是 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝你平安，我们下一集再见。
